value-type-mismatch.json.reason: rule 3: a value failing its declared value_type is a producer rejection; the read path does no value typing (spec/value-types.md), so the reader folds the op with the value intact

undeclared-op-type.json.reason: rule 4: an op_type the schema does not declare for this object_type is a producer rejection; a reader has no matching rule and reports UnknownOp

undeclared-op-version.json.reason: rule 4: an op_version the schema does not declare for this op_type is a producer rejection; a reader has no matching rule and reports UnknownOp

undeclared-object-type.json.reason: tier 4: an object_type no schema in the log declares is refused at the producer; a reader falls through the absent-schema path to UnknownOp (FC-1, spec/schema-ops.md 7.1)

contested-object-type.json.reason: tier 3 (the ruling's carve-out): two schema objects binding the same qualified object_type install no rules (spec/schema-ops.md 6), so the write is permitted unvalidated while the reader still reports UnknownOp -- the write/read asymmetry is the point

declared-type-with-no-fields.json.reason: tier 2 is decided from the declared-type set, not from a non-empty rules slice: a type declared by define-op alone (no define-field) accepts an op of its declared op type with an empty body; with no field rules installed at all, a reader has nothing to fold and reports UnknownOp

deprecated-field-still-writable.json.reason: deprecated is metadata discouraging new writes, never a filter (spec/schema-ops.md 5, 8): the field rule stays installed and active for both the producer and the fold

keyed-lww-key-column.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214): a keyed-lww field's key column is declared by being a member of key on the field's own rule, not by a separate field rule of its own, so a body carrying both the field and its key column is accepted at the producer and interpretable by the reader

keyed-lww-key-column-not-a-string.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214): a keyed-lww key column's value MUST be a JSON string regardless of its key_types entry, because fold treats a non-string key component as uninterpretable (spec/fold.md §5 keyed-lww); this is the lockstep pin -- a producer refusal matched by a reader quarantine, not the interpretable-but-wrong tolerance an ordinary value_type mismatch gets

keyed-lww-key-column-null.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 2): JSON null is not a JSON string, so a keyed-lww key column carrying null is rejected the same as any other non-string key column value -- unlike an ordinary declared field, where null is tolerated as a legitimate 'no write', a key column addresses a register rather than carrying a value of its own and fold's keyed-lww strategy does not tolerate null there either

keyed-lww-key-column-enum.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 2): an enum-typed key column is held to the JSON-string requirement and nothing more, because key_types (a column -> catalogue type name map) has no slot for the member list an enum field's own enum attribute would supply -- accepting a value outside any particular field's declared enum members is correct here, not a hole, since key_types carries no member list to check membership against in the first place

keyed-lww-key-column-also-a-field-not-a-.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 3): where a name is both a declared field (here, seq int lww) and another rule's keyed-lww key column (verdict's key(seq string)), the field rule governs the value's declared type, but the key column's JSON-string floor still applies on top -- a JSON number satisfying the field's int type is not a JSON string, so the producer refuses it just as fold.ruleAccepts would quarantine it; byField winning outright, as it did before this fix, let a JSON number through and left the reader to quarantine it alone

keyed-lww-key-column-int.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 3): an int-typed key column's JSON-string content is the decimal encoding of the integer, exactly as spec/schema-ops.md §3.1 already requires for op_version -- "7" decodes to the JSON integer 7 and typechecks against value_type int, so the field is writable rather than permanently rejecting every value the way calling value.Validate on the raw string did

keyed-lww-key-column-int-invalid-encodin.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 3): a key column string whose content is not valid JSON at all, let alone a JSON integer, fails the producer's int decode -- but fold never decodes key-column content (only isString), so the read path folds the op with the key component intact, same asymmetry as value-type-mismatch.json

keyed-lww-key-column-int-non-canonical.j.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 4): "7.0" decodes to the same JSON integer as "7", but it is not that integer's canonical decimal spelling (spec/op-envelope.md's "decimal string" language, spec/schema-ops.md §3.1's op_version precedent) -- fold keys a keyed-lww register on the raw string, so admitting every spelling that merely parses would let two producers who mean the same key write to registers that never converge. The producer now requires the content to already be canonicaljson's own encoding of itself; the reader still only checks isString, so it folds the op with the non-canonical key component intact, same asymmetry as keyed-lww-key-column-int-invalid-encoding.json

keyed-lww-key-column-also-a-field-int-de.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 4): where a name is both a declared field (here, seq int lww) and another rule's keyed-lww key column typed int, the key-column JSON-string floor and the field's own int value_type are jointly satisfiable once the field-rule branch decodes the string's content the same way validateKeyColumnValue already does for a key-column-only name -- "7" decodes to the JSON integer 7, which the field's own value_type int accepts, so the field is writable instead of every value being permanently refused

keyed-lww-key-column-also-a-field-int-no.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 4): the same dual-role int field/key-column still refuses a raw JSON number -- it satisfies the field's own int value_type but fails the key-column JSON-string floor every keyed-lww key column carries regardless of key_types, which fold.ruleAccepts also refuses (isString(7) is false), so the reader quarantines the op as unknown

keyed-lww-key-column-also-a-field-tombst.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 5): where a name is both a declared field with strategy tombstone (here, flag bool tombstone) and another rule's keyed-lww key column, no value ever satisfies both roles at once -- fold's tombstone reducer requires the raw body value to already be a JSON boolean, while the key-column floor requires the same body value to be a JSON string, and a JSON value cannot be both. A rule combination no value can ever satisfy is refused where the schema resolves (spec/schema-ops.md §8): the resolver withholds both rules and reports one SchemaConflict, so this schema declares no rule for (approve, 1) at all and the producer rejects the body as undeclared rather than letting the field be declarable and then unwritable. The reader has no matching rule either, so it reports the op as unknown

keyed-lww-key-column-timestamp.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 5): a timestamp-typed key column's value is already a JSON string with no content to decode, but it must also already be in its instant's one canonical spelling -- UTC ("Z"), fractional seconds only when nonzero and with no trailing zero digits -- so "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" is accepted as written

keyed-lww-key-column-timestamp-non-canon.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 5): "2024-01-01T01:00:00+01:00" names the same instant as "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" but is a different byte string, and fold keys a keyed-lww register on the byte string (value.Normalize is the identity for timestamp), so admitting every RFC 3339 spelling of an instant would let two producers who mean the same key address registers that never converge. The producer now requires the canonical UTC spelling; the reader still only checks isString, so it folds the op with the non-canonical key component intact, the same asymmetry keyed-lww-key-column-int-non-canonical.json pins for int

keyed-lww-key-column-absent.json.reason: rule 5 (WRIT-219): a body writing a keyed-lww field must carry every column of that field's declared key, or the op folds onto the empty key and the field's declared per-key partition silently degenerates to plain lww with no error at any layer -- a body carrying "verdict" alone, with its declared key column "subject" entirely absent, is now a producer rejection. keyed-lww-key-column-partially-absent.js.reason: rule 5 (WRIT-219): the same rule fires on a partially-absent key, not only a wholly-absent one -- "verdict" is keyed on (subject, revision) and the body carries "subject" but omits "revision", so the producer refuses it naming the missing column. The single-column-key version of this fixture passed vacuously: its one key column doubled as the very column a wrongly-scoped rule 5 would already find present, so it stayed green even with the body[r.Field] guard removed. A two-column key with the field absent and only one column present discriminates: an implementation that checked every keyed-lww rule's columns unconditionally, instead of scoping to rules whose field the body writes, would refuse this body for lacking "revision" -- so this fixture only passes when rule 5 is scoped correctly

keyed-lww-rule-scoped-by-op-type.json.reason: rule 5 (WRIT-219 round 2) negative control: "verdict" is keyed-lww key(subject) under op_type "review", but this envelope writes op_type "approve", whose own "verdict" rule is plain lww with no key at all -- cross-op-type field-name reuse is ordinary (WRIT-198). The body carries "verdict" alone and is accepted, because rule 5 draws its rule set from the op's own (op_type, op_version) the way rule 3 already does, not from every keyed-lww rule the schema declares anywhere; a reading of rule 5 as "any keyed-lww rule this schema declares" would wrongly refuse this body for lacking "subject", a key column belonging to a different op type's rule entirely
